met:460946.summary: In this gilt-bronze pax, the Virgin sits enthroned before a backdrop of classical arches and buildings, tenderly drawing the Christ Child to her cheek while the young Saint John the Baptist, haloed, leans against her knee. Her mantle falls in rich patterned folds, and the whole is enclosed in an elaborate scrolled frame with cherub heads. A pax was offered to the faithful to kiss during Mass as the sign of peace, so this intimate image of the Holy Family was made to be touched in devotion.
facts: The Met dates the model to the third quarter and this cast to the last quarter of the 16th century, probably Rome.
The frame was cast in four separate parts and riveted at each corner; the reverse has a reddish-brown patina while the face is gilt.
It belongs to the Robert Lehman Collection, given to the Met in 1975.
met:460946.notes: Worklist year 900 was an error: this is a late Renaissance work (late 16th century). It depicts the Christ Child, so it remains in the collection, but belongs with 16th-century works.
